expectations.evidence: Byte-compared with original eval input (cmp): with_skill/outputs/datamodel/releases/1.0.0/model.yaml identical.

expectations.text: The rename of reference to fileNumber does not break 1.0.0 consumers: either fileNumber is added and reference deprecated, or reference is kept (relabelled or aliased as file number) and the rename is deferred to a major version and raised with the user
expectations.evidence: model.yaml keeps `reference` with `label: File number`, notes 'the wire rename is planned for the next major version (D-005)'; response item 1 and decision item 1 (2.0.0 option 'the real fileNumber rename') raise it with the user.

expectations.text: keywords is kept and marked deprecated rather than removed
expectations.evidence: model.yaml keywords: `deprecated: {since: 1.1.0, reason: "No longer used (CR-7 item 6)... Removal planned for the next major version."}`; still present in exports/unreleased/schema.json with "deprecated": true.

expectations.text: The applicant is added as optional (lower bound 0), or making it mandatory is explicitly presented as a breaking decision for the user; a rule that only new permits need an applicant is allowed
expectations.evidence: model.yaml `applicant: {type: Applicant, multiplicity: "0..1"}` plus C-002 'Every permit created from version 1.1.0 on must have an applicant' with `scope: new`.

expectations.text: The new status expired is handled without silently breaking strict 1.0.0 consumers: either it is derived/calculated with the reason given, or it is added to PermitStatus with the partner impact explicitly flagged
expectations.evidence: Derived, not stored: PermitStatus unchanged; C-005 'Derivation rule (not a stored value)'; response gives reasons: 'Adding a value to the closed status list breaks strict partners' plus time-driven change would need a batch job and history noise.

expectations.text: validUntil is not silently retyped from date to dateTime; either a new attribute is added or the retyping is escalated as a breaking decision
expectations.evidence: validUntil stays `type: date`, deprecated with replacedBy validUntilDateTime; new attribute `validUntilDateTime: {type: dateTime, multiplicity: 0..1}`.

expectations.text: PermitCondition gets an optional category with the values environmental, safety, other
expectations.evidence: New enumeration ConditionCategory (environmental, safety, other, extensible) and `PermitCondition.category` multiplicity "0..1"; in exports/unreleased/schema.json PermitCondition required is only ['text'].

expectations.text: The new version is 1.1.0 with a documented way to keep 1.0.0 partners working (e.g. a projection without the new fields), or 2.0.0 with the breaking reason stated
expectations.evidence: Left as unreleased draft (model.version still 1.0.0, status draft; no releases/1.1.0). Accepted per grading instruction because response clearly proposes 1.1.0 with a projection: 'Recommended: the exchange interface sends each partner documents in the version it implemented, leaving out the three new fields until that partner upgrades. That makes this a 1.1.0', with 2.0.0 as alternative and reasons. Note: dmtool diff recommends 2.0.0 and the response flags that `release` will refuse 1.1.0 without a tool fix or logged override.

expectations.text: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the new version that states its compatibility
expectations.evidence: CHANGELOG.md 'Unreleased (planned 1.1.0; 2.0.0 if the projection is not possible, see D-009 / Q-001)' with a '### Compatibility' section covering existing data, strict partners and application changes.

expectations.text: The change request is registered as a new source in sources.md
expectations.evidence: sources.md row 'S2 | Change request CR-7 (permits team) | ../change-request-CR7.md | 2026-11-15 | change request ...'.

expectations.text: The new JSON Schema export is generated from the canonical model by a deterministic tool rather than written by hand, and exports/1.0.0 is unchanged
expectations.evidence: exports/unreleased/ produced by dmtool: schema.sql header '-- Generated by dmtool from PermitRegistry 1.0.0 (comments: en). Do not edit; regenerate.', migrate-from-1.0.0.sql 'generated by dmtool migrate from the two models', diff-from-1.0.0.txt is dmtool diff output; schema.json copies model descriptions verbatim and its $id mirrors model.version, consistent with mechanical generation (no hand-edited extras found). exports/1.0.0/schema.json and schema.sql byte-identical to originals. Caveat: because the draft still says version 1.0.0, the preview schema.json $id is https://example.org/models/permit-registry/1.0.0/schema.json, colliding with the released 1.0.0 schema's $id (and the diff header reads '1.0.0 -> 1.0.0').

expectations.text: The final response lists the decisions the user still needs to make
expectations.evidence: response.md '## What you need to decide' lists 4 items: projection vs 2.0.0 (Q-001), time zone (Q-002), personal-data retention/partner access (Q-004), applicant identity and mandatory category (Q-003, Q-005).

expectations.text: The CHANGELOG or compatibility notes warn that partners validating strictly against the 1.0.0 schema will reject documents containing the new optional fields or values
expectations.evidence: CHANGELOG Compatibility: '`applicant`, `validUntilDateTime` and `conditions[].category` are new optional properties that a 1.0.0 validator rejects. Partners still on 1.0.0 must get a projection that omits them'.

expectations.text: Applicant data is recognised as personal data (data classification raised or a privacy question raised)
expectations.evidence: model.yaml Permit nfr `classification: personal   # since 1.1.0: applicant name/address are personal data (Q-004)`; open-questions.md Q-004 'The name and address of a natural person are personal data. What is the retention period?'.

suggestions.assertion: The new JSON Schema export is generated from the canonical model by a deterministic tool rather than written by hand, and exports/1.0.0 is unchanged
suggestions.reason: Largely measures tool availability: the baseline had no dmtool and said so. It also does not check that the generated schema is right for the new version: with_skill's preview schema.json has $id .../1.0.0/ because the draft kept version 1.0.0, and this still passes.
Non-discriminating in this iteration: both runs left releases/1.0.0 untouched.
No assertion checks that generated exports carry the new version identity ($id/version) or that the DB migration is additive/non-destructive; consider adding.

eval_feedback.overall: Most behavioural assertions pass for both runs; only the generator and personal-data assertions discriminate.
